title: Learned reaction models guide improved yields for three ester hydrogenations
summary: Learned models of ruthenium-catalysed ester hydrogenation guided laboratory condition choices for four previously studied substrates. Three experiments gave higher alcohol yields than the corresponding literature conditions; a fourth failed despite a high predicted yield. The result is a limited improvement of known reactions, rather than a new catalyst, transformation or universally accurate yield predictor.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process regression and comparative learned reaction models
organization: University of Cambridge; Université Paris Cité; University of St Andrews

evidence.tested: The journal paper reports measured alcohol yields of 96%,63% and 99% compared with corresponding literature values of 3%,0% and 32%. The fourth experiment yielded below 1% despite an 84% model prediction.
evidence.unknown: An earlier matching preprint,10.26434/chemrxiv-2022-t1zsn, is dated January 10,2022; its full original body was not authenticated, so this record uses the documented May 1,2023 journal version and does not claim first public priority. The substrates and catalysts were known; improvements concern these conditions, not new chemical entities or general catalyst superiority. Prediction errors and high-yield-biased data limit generalization.
evidence.ai_role: Learned regressors map substrate/catalyst descriptors and reaction conditions to measured yield and guide new condition choices subsequently tested in the laboratory.

source_review.scope: Full primary author-deposited journal PDF front, learned-model Methods, experimental validation and Table2; exact matching preprint relationship and current Crossref status. Journal-version result represented; original preprint result content not asserted.
